item.title: The Sch\"urmann-Vallentin lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering in dimension six
item.description: arXiv:2611.28562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ discovered by Sch\"urmann and Vallentin in 2006 is the unique (up to similarity) six-dimensional lattice that gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Garber

item.title: The Z[tau]-foam: Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam as arithmetic in the icosahedral module
item.description: arXiv:2611.28955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam is a substitution that fills the regular dodecahedron with dodecahedral bubbles of sizes tau^{-k}, tau=(1+sqrt(5))/2, using the seven kinds of cells into which the twelve planes of its stellation cut it. We rewrite it as exact arithmetic in one Z[tau]-module of rank three, the span M of the six five-fold axes, on which the icosahedral group acts by 120 matrices in GL(3,Z[tau]). A placed inflated copy of a cell is a union of cells iff its facet levels lie in {+-1,+-tau^3} and it lies in the dodecahedron. Solving this finite linear system for all scales at once gives exactly the 22 rules known from a geometric search; no rule exists at any scale other than 1,tau,tau^2,tau^3. The substitution becomes integer arithmetic on six-tuples and reproduces the bubbles of the geometric foam exactly. Whether a point of M is the centre of a bubble of size tau^{-k} is decided by at most k+3 exact sign vectors (its address), without building the foam, and all bubbles of one size are obtained by sieving the points of M whose Galois conjugate satisfies |x^*|<=2 tau^k, a bound we prove with computer assistance. The number of bubbles of size tau^{-k} is A beta^k+O(|beta'|^k) with beta=(1+sqrt(29))/2. Hence the closure of the rescaled conjugates of the bubble centres has box dimension at most log_tau(beta)=2.4123<3, and the bubbles are not selected by any cut-and-project window with interior. The other foams of the 1999 article are sub-foams of this one. The 50400 substitutions allowed by the rule list give 18899 bubble sets, and the Dodecafoam is a product set of 13440 of them, to the depth tested. In four dimensions the same linear system, for the star cut of the 120-cell, reproduces the 718 clusters of a geometric search and adds the scale sqrt(5) tau^2.
item.dc:creator: Miguel E. P\'erez Ibarra, Jaziel Flores Rodr\'iguez

item.title: Economic cap coverings for log-concave measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.29013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mu$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Write $q_\mu$ for its half-space depth, $W_t=\{q_\mu \leqslant t\}$ for its wet part, and $w_\mu(t)=\mu(W_t)$. For sufficiently small $t$, we construct a cover of $W_t$ by half-spaces of measure at most $A_nt$, with cardinality bounded by $$D_n\frac{w_\mu(t)-w_\mu(a_nt)}{t},$$ where the constants depend only on $n$. For each $0<\varepsilon\leqslant 1$ we also construct a cover by half-spaces of measure at most $(1+\varepsilon)t$, with cardinality bounded by $$B_n\varepsilon^{-(n-1)/2}\frac{w_\mu(t)-w_\mu(a_nt)}{t}.$$ The exponent $(n-1)/2$ is optimal for $n\geqslant 2$, as shown by the Gaussian example. We further establish containment coverings for half-spaces in every dimension: there is a family of $O_n(w_\mu(t)/t)$ Borel covering sets, each of $\mu$-measure $O_n(t)$, such that every half-space of measure at most $t$ is contained in one covering set. We also obtain a relative wet-part estimate with sharp exponent $2/(n+1)$ and a reverse doubling inequality.
item.dc:creator: Minas Pafis

item.title: Plane Curves Whose Curvature Is a Function of the Distance to the Tangent Line: Relations Between Karpenkov's Areal and Angular Densities
item.description: arXiv:2611.29065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a plane curve and a point $O$, O. Karpenkov introduced the areal density $A$ and the angular density $B$ as smooth counterparts of the alternating entries of an LLS sequence. Here $A$ is the signed distance from $O$ to the tangent line, and, with the order of the chords in the signed definition fixed here, $A^2B=\kappa$, where $\kappa$ is the signed curvature. A relation between the two densities therefore prescribes the curvature as a function of the distance to the tangent line. Karpenkov asked which curves have $AB$, or $B$ alone, constant. The equation $AB=C$ gives the shrinking, stationary and expanding profiles of planar curve shortening. For constant nonzero $B$, choose the orientation so that $B>0$. Curves with positive support have periodic support or are centred circles. The noncircular closed curves are classified by their turning fractions in $(1/2,1/\sqrt3)$; the centred circle is the only embedded closed solution. Negative support gives smooth open graphs whose two ends approach rays from the origin. On positive support the polar reciprocal is a constant-force orbit, and the original curve is a rotated and scaled velocity curve of that orbit. For $A^3B=C$ we determine which ends extend to infinity, reach a cusp, or spiral into the origin. We describe regularity and the range of turning fractions for the positive-support family $A^pB=C$. Finally, for a general relation $B=\Phi(A)$ the polar reciprocal is an orbit of the central force $L^2/\Phi(1/r)$; we describe the ends of all arcs with $AB<0$ and show that a closed curve with turning fraction $m/n$ has exactly $n(m-1)$ double points. We also describe the curves whose areal or angular density is a linear function of the arclength.
item.dc:creator: Esther Notik

item.title: Area Stability for Largest Small Polygons
item.description: arXiv:2611.29185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a second order calculus for area maximisation among small polygons of diameter at most one, culminating in rigorous computational proofs of stationarity, spectral stability and strict local maximality modulo orientation preserving Euclidean motions for the polygons $Q_n$, whose diameter graphs consist of a cycle on $n-1$ vertices and one pendant edge, for every even $n$ with $6\le n\le 64$. At a stationary configuration, positive multipliers force first order area decrease along feasible directions that shorten at least one active diameter. Along directions that preserve all active diameters to first order, the reduced Hessian governs second order area change modulo Euclidean motions. Positive multipliers, independent active constraint gradients, and a negative reduced spectrum imply strict local maximality. Outward rounded interval arithmetic establishes existence of strictly convex stationary configurations $Q_n$ with all $n-3$ reduced eigenvalues strictly negative. Together, these results yield explicit neighbourhood radii and rigorous quadratic area decrease bounds for all sufficiently nearby feasible polygons. The reduced spectrum also detects second order degeneracy and instability, as illustrated by an optimal quadrilateral and the regular hexagon.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Ayala Hoffmann, Joaqu\'in L\'opez Guti\'errez

item.title: Sharp Volume Contraction of a Centrally Cut John Ellipsoid
item.description: arXiv:2611.29323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ in positive dimension, let $w(K)$ be the volume of its maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid. For a closed halfspace $H$ whose boundary passes through the center of that ellipsoid, we prove \[ w(K\cap H)\le R_nw(K),\qquad R_1=\frac12,\qquad R_n=\frac12\left(\frac n{n-1}\right)^{(n-1)/2}\quad(n\ge2), \] with equality attained in every fixed dimension. This refines the optimal dimension-independent bound from the author's earlier work on [Khachiyan's ellipsoid conjecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28447). We characterize the full equality family, including nonsimplex extremizers, and establish an exact volume-deficit identity that yields dimension-independent stability of the new ellipsoid and its weighted contact geometry in John coordinates. The proof reduces the problem to finite John contacts and constructs an explicit conic certificate by a transformation of contact directions and a common polar rotation. Its determinant is controlled by a nonnegative contact defect. The sharp contraction theorem, equality classification, stability estimates, and supporting results have been formally verified in Lean 4 using mathlib.
item.dc:creator: Zhou Longfei

item.title: Scaling cores and dust-free layered sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.29446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Hausdorff-box dimension gaps in compact sets of finite positive Hausdorff measure. At each scale, the points of low local measure form a scaling core that carries all covering growth above the Hausdorff dimension. This gives gap criteria for both box and intermediate dimensions. We construct dust-free layered sets, in which every neighbourhood of every point has positive measure. Their dimensions are determined by the layer dimension and a product core formed from a horizontal limit set and a sequence of heights. Under a suitable approximation-rate condition, the volume remaining after subtraction of the product tube grows linearly with radius, with coefficient twice the total layer measure. Every compact null horizontal set admits such a construction. Cantor approximants, homogeneous cube constructions and Bedford-McMullen carpets illustrate the results.
item.dc:creator: Sini\v{s}a Mili\v{c}i\'{c}

item.title: Distinct Distances under Well-behaved Norms
item.description: arXiv:2611.29686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We improve our understanding of the Erdos' distinct distances problem under non-Euclidean norms, in two ways: (i) For norms that are definable in an o-minimal structure and whose non-line bisectors have a finite intersection, we obtain a lower bound of \(\Omega(n^{5/6})\) for the minimum number of distinct distances. In particular, this improves the current best bound of \(\Omega(n^{4/5})\) for all \(\ell_{p}\) norms with non-integer \(p > 1\). (ii) We derive the stronger bound \(\Omega(n^{6/7-\epsilon})\) under all semi-algebraic smooth norms. Our proof technique is based on deriving properties of bisectors under various norms.
item.dc:creator: Lillian MacArthur, Adam Sheffer

item.title: Second Moment Penny Packings via Rolling Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.29844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve the unrestricted minimum second moment problem for six unit disks in the plane by proving that the minimum is \(29/3\) attained uniquely up to isometry and relabelling by one disk together with five of its six neighbours in the triangular lattice. The realised contacts themselves define the space of admissible motions, while the directions preserving those contacts to first order define the rolling space consisting of motions whose relative velocities have zero normal component at every realised contact. Together, these spaces lead to an exact tangent cone formula and to a criterion by which a strictly positive centroidal contact balance, combined with rolling rigidity, implies strict local minimality modulo Euclidean motions. Our method recovers the classical five disk minimum \(34/5\) of Graham and Sloane, previously the largest unrestricted case known exactly. Geometric reductions and a graph census reduce the global search to finitely many contact graph classes. Exact analysis and validated interval arithmetic then exclude competing configurations, establishing the global bounds and uniqueness. Our method allows us to pass from putative lattice extremisers to unrestricted optimality.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Ayala Hoffmann, Fabi\'an Henry Vilaxa

item.title: Maximal sections of the cube
item.description: arXiv:2611.30144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the folklore conjecture on maximal central sections of the cube in every dimension and codimension. The maximizing sections are exactly the products of diagonals of disjoint coordinate blocks whose sizes differ by at most one. This determines the sharp volume in the cases left open by Ball's 1989 bounds. In fixed dimensions, the logarithmic volume deficit controls both the direction and the displacement of an affine section linearly, with optimal exponent. We also obtain the sharp uniform bound on projection densities for independent real random variables with bounded densities.
item.dc:creator: Vu Khac Ky

item.title: Restrictions of planar doubling measures to piecewise C1 Jordan domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.30571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare the class $\mathscr R(\Omega)$ of restrictions of full-support planar doubling measures with the class $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ of internal doubling measures on a piecewise $C^1$ Jordan domain. These classes coincide in the absence of zero-interior-angle cusps. At any such cusp, $\mathscr R(\Omega)\setminus\mathcal D(\Omega)$ is nonempty. For power-comparable widths, $\mathcal D(\Omega)\subsetneq\mathscr R(\Omega)$; for infinitely flat widths the two classes are disjoint. Under smooth endpoint regularity, finite versus infinite contact order gives these two alternatives. Under only $C^1$ regularity, finite logarithmic order does not determine whether the classes intersect, and examples with nonempty intersection and neither class containing the other also occur. For an individual internal measure, membership in $\mathscr R(\Omega)$ is characterized by a potential inequality for its axial projection. We prove this criterion by a positive-kernel construction and Whitney mass replacement, and also obtain sufficient conditions for variable-power widths and an independent finite-system criterion.
item.dc:creator: Xiaohua Wang, Fan Wen

item.title: The Boundary Conjecture for Smoothable Alexandrov Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.30860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that in a noncollapsed limit of complete Riemannian manifolds with $\sec\ge\kappa$, each boundary component of a compact full-dimensional convex body, equipped with its intrinsic length metric, has Alexandrov curvature at least $\kappa$. We also consider such a body in the limit of a noncollapsed sequence of Alexandrov spaces with curvature at least $\kappa$. If $\kappa>0$ or the boundary of the body is strongly convex, we show that the body can be approximated by convex bodies in the given sequence.
item.dc:creator: Nina Lebedeva

item.title: $C^{m,\alpha}$-rectifiability in Carnot groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.30960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In an arbitrary Carnot group $\mathbb{G}$ of homogeneous dimension $Q$, we characterize rectifiability of sets of finite Hausdorff measure by $\mathbf C_{\mathbb{G}}^{m,\alpha}$-regular surfaces with complemented vertical tangent subgroups, for every $m\ge1$ and $\alpha\in[0,1]$. The criterion combines positive lower density with approximation in measure by tubes around such surfaces. At almost every point, one tube radius $\lambda r^{m+\alpha}$ suffices for $\alpha>0$, whereas the estimate must hold for every $\lambda r^m$, $\lambda>0$, for $\alpha=0$. Tubular approximation upgrades $\mathbf C^1_{\mathbb{G}}$-rectifiability to class $(m,\alpha)$ without an additional density assumption. The proof combines ambient normal-form polynomial jets, a Remez-type norming inequality, and Whitney extension. In topological dimension at least two, quantitative volume approximation by noncharacteristic sublevel sets yields higher-order rectifiability of reduced boundaries. In particular, for weak solutions of the horizontal Poisson equation with $L^q_{\mathrm{loc}}$ forcing ($q>\max\{Q,2\}$ finite), almost every sublevel set has second-order rectifiable reduced boundary.
item.dc:creator: Kennedy Obinna Idu, Francesco Paolo Maiale

item.title: Quotient maps, pliability, and Lusin approximation in Carnot groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.31017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Carnot groups, we show that pliability and the Lusin approximation property are preserved by quotient maps, and we deduce several applications. For instance, we show that, in free Carnot groups of step at least 3 with at least $2$ generators, every horizontal direction is non-pliable, the Lusin property fails in a strong sense, and there is a Lipschitz curve that is purely unrectifiable with respect to smooth horizontal curves. We also give a previously unpublished example of a pliable Carnot group, namely, the group of upper triangular, unipotent matrices.
item.dc:creator: Gareth Speight, Scott Zimmerman

item.title: When Positivity Matters: Maximal Distance Integrals on Curves and Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.31045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How far apart, on average, can $n$ points in a set $A$ be? As $n\to\infty$ the answer is the $\textit{maximal energy}$ $M^{+}(A)$, the largest possible value of $\mathbb{E}|X-Y|$ when $X$ and $Y$ are independent random points of $A$ with a common distribution. If the distribution is allowed to carry negative mass, we obtain a second constant $M(A)\ge M^{+}(A)$. It is often far easier to compute: when a signed equilibrium measure exists, it is characterized by a $\textit{linear}$ potential equation, whereas the positive problem must also locate the support of the mass. This paper asks when positivity matters, that is, when $M^{+}(A)<M(A)$. For polygons and polyhedra the extremal mass sits on the vertices and closed forms abound. Even so, every hollow convex polygon has $M^{+}<M$, and a simple kite shows how a vertex can be forced out of the support. For smooth curves and surfaces the answer depends on the shape. Circles and spheres have $M^{+}=M$. The ellipse $x^2+4y^2=4$ has $M^{+}=M$ numerically, and we give its value to 50 digits. The ellipses $x^2+9y^2=9$ and $x^2+25y^2=25$ have $M^{+}<M$ numerically, with gaps in the support. For the ellipsoid $10x^2+15y^2+12z^2=15$, studied by Larcher, Schmid and Wolf, we compute 50 digits of $M$ and give strong numerical evidence that $M^{+}<M$. The extremal measure vanishes on two caps around the ends of the shortest axis. Proofs and numerical methods are collected in appendices.
item.dc:creator: Steven Finch

item.title: Wet-part doubling for log-concave probability measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.29020v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mu$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geqslant 2$. We study the growth of $w_\mu(t)=\mu(\{x:q_{\mu}(x)\leqslant t\})$, where $q_{\mu}$ is the Tukey half-space depth function of $\mu$. We prove that $w_{\mu}$ satisfies the doubling bound $$w_\mu(\lambda t)\leqslant C^n\lambda\left(1+\frac{\log\lambda}{n-1}\right)^{n-1}w_\mu(t)$$ for every $\lambda>1$ and $0<t<1/\lambda$, where $C>0$ is an absolute constant. It follows that for every $\varepsilon>0$ we may write $w_\mu(\lambda t) \leqslant A_\varepsilon^n \lambda^{1+\varepsilon}w_\mu(t)$ for some constant $A_\varepsilon>0$. We construct a family of symmetric log-concave measures in every dimension $n\geqslant2$ showing that no linear doubling bound with a dimension-dependent constant holds uniformly over this class. The proof of the doubling bound uses a pointwise comparison of half-space depth with the Cram\'{e}r transform, dual radial coordinates, and a relative entropy estimate for transverse covariance determinants.
item.dc:creator: Apostolos Giannopoulos, Minas Pafis

item.title: Almost-Isometric Embeddings of Graphs into Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.29469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graphs represent objects as vertices and relationships as edges; positive edge weights define shortest-path metrics. Metric embeddings leverage target-space geometry to analyze distances. Foundational results target linear spaces: Nash embedded Riemannian manifolds isometrically into Euclidean space, and Bourgain embedded $n$-point metrics into Hilbert space with $O(\log n)$ distortion. By contrast, the manifold hypothesis places high-dimensional data near low-dimensional smooth manifolds, making such manifolds themselves target spaces. What distortion is needed to embed a finite graph metric into such a manifold with its intrinsic distance? Although the star $K_{1,3}$ cannot embed isometrically into any complete Riemannian manifold, we prove almost-isometric embeddings always exist: for $\varepsilon>0$ and any finite connected positively weighted graph, we construct a smooth connected closed orientable surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ admitting a noncontractive $(1+\varepsilon)$-embedding of its vertices, with $\varepsilon$ arbitrarily small and independent of graph parameters. This construction transfers communication schemes between graphs and surfaces. For independent unicasts, fractional routing splits flows across paths while network coding lets relays combine messages. Space information flow permits relays anywhere, charging bandwidth times distance. Whereas coding advantage (optimal routing over coding cost) equals one in Euclidean space, we prove coding advantages on finite positively weighted undirected graphs transfer to smooth closed surfaces within factors approaching one. Counterexamples to the multiple-unicast conjecture and amplification yield smooth closed surfaces with unbounded coding advantage. Conversely, coding advantage is at most $C\log(g+2)$ on finite undirected graphs of orientable genus $g$ and smooth closed orientable surfaces of genus $g$, for absolute $C$.
item.dc:creator: Sirui Liu, Zongpeng Li, Baochun Li

item.title: Qualitative WALA, Alberti representations and Lipschitz differentiability
item.description: arXiv:2611.29700v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the existing theory of Lipschitz differentiability spaces implies that a metric measure space satisfying a qualitative analogue of the WALA condition of David--Semmes has many independent Alberti representations, and provides conditions for when such a space is rectifiable.
item.dc:creator: David Bate

item.title: Circle-Pattern Linear Systems for the Twenty Trivalent Delaunay Types of a Genus-Two Surface: Rank, Feasibility and Polytope Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.29848v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The hyperelliptic quotient of a closed genus-two Riemann surface is a hyperbolic sphere with six cone points of angle pi. Its Delaunay triangulation T is dual to a trivalent Voronoi graph G of one of twenty combinatorial types. For each type we study the angle system Ax = 1, x >= 0, where A is the vertex-edge incidence matrix of T and pi x_e is the angle subtended at a cone point by the Voronoi edge dual to e, equivalently the intersection angle of the two circumcircles adjacent across e. We prove that rank A = 6 for all twenty types, including the six whose triangulation has a loop, so the affine solution space always has the dimension of Teichmuller space. The polytope P = {Ax = 1, x >= 0} behaves differently. It is six-dimensional for exactly ten types, the ten Delaunay-realizable ones. For nine types it has dimension one, two or three, because non-negativity forces some wedge angles to vanish, and for the type of signature (2,2,2,2,8,8) it is empty. We show that five of the nine and the empty type never occur as Delaunay triangulations, and that the other four occur only as triangulations of non-trivalent Delaunay decompositions. Every vertex of every P is half-integral, as for fractional perfect matching polytopes. For the ten full-dimensional types every facet x_e = 0 lies at an edge where the Whitehead move is admissible, though not conversely, and the move identifies the facets of the two polytopes; these identifications pair the facet orbits of the ten cells under their automorphism groups. The free unfolding of the gluing grows at rate about 7.093. All finite statements are checked by an independent program, and the rank, infeasibility, forced coordinates, dimensions, vertices and facets are verified in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Armando Rodado Amaris

item.title: Connected Lie groups with a left-invariant intrinsic chronometer
item.description: arXiv:2611.30995v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate left-invariant intrinsic chronometers (time functions) on connected finite-dimensional Lie groups. We formulate and prove sub-Lorentzian analogs of V.\,N.\,Berestovskii's classical direct and inverse theorems. A one-to-one correspondence is established between chronometers satisfying the proposed system of axioms (including upper semi-continuity and the condition that the interiors of chronological rhombi form a base for the topology) and smooth left-invariant sub-Lorentzian structures. It is shown that an axiomatic chronometer uniquely determines a closed, pointed, convex cone in the Lie algebra, whose linear span satisfies the Chow--Rashevskii condition, and an upper semi-continuous concave positively homogeneous anti-norm on it. Conversely, it is proved that any such algebraic structure satisfying a local chronologicity condition induces an intrinsic chronometer with the required properties. The proofs rely on local estimates in exponential coordinates, the Hahn--Banach separation theorem, and properties of weak limits in optimal control problems.
item.dc:creator: Ramazan G. Beden

item.title: Harmonic functions near isolated subanalytic singularities: generalized horns and regular blow-up
item.description: arXiv:2611.31091v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a subanalytic set of dimension $d\ge 2$, closed near $0$, with an isolated singularity at $0$ and connected link, whose regular part carries the induced Riemannian metric. We study harmonic functions on $X\setminus\{0\}$ near $0$. (i) If $X$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent, for the intrinsic metric, to a generalized horn $\{(z^\gamma y,z):\ y\in L,\ z\ge 0\}$, with $\gamma\ge 1$ rational and $L$ compact, connected, subanalytic and analytic, then: - every bounded harmonic function extends continuously to $0$; - every positive harmonic function near $0$ can be written as $qG_X+u_b$, with $q\ge 0$, $u_b$ bounded and $G_X$ a fixed singular profile; - a B\^ocher-type theorem holds: a positive harmonic function is either bounded or tends to $+\infty$, and two divergent ones have a nontrivial linear combination that extends continuously. The proof relies on a volume doubling and weak Poincar\'e condition on intrinsic balls away from $0$, invariant under bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms, which together with an annular connectedness condition implies a Harnack inequality on annuli; the decomposition then follows from a Picard-principle argument whose geometric input is the Harnack inequality on the links. (ii) If $d\ge 3$ and the spherical blow-up of $X$ at $0$ is a regular manifold with boundary parametrizing $X$ near $0$ (condition (R) of the paper), the singular profile has a polyhomogeneous expansion, which is described and may contain a $\log\rho$ term, $\rho=|x|$. (iii) For the rotational cusps $|x|^2=z^m$, $m>2$, $d\ge 3$, whose spherical blow-up is not regular, the profile is radial of order $\rho^{1-m(d-1)/2}$, so that its exponent depends on the rate at which the sections shrink.
item.dc:creator: Flavio Mosca

item.title: Regular polygons
item.dc:creator: J. Mainik

item.title: Self-similar dendrites with finite boundary and P-sprouts
item.description: arXiv:2605.11833v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Each self-similar dendrite K with a finite self-similar boundary defines a finite acyclic edge-labeled bipartite graph G, called the sprout of K. The paper shows that the sprout G determines the combinatorial properties of the dendrite K and its topological structure.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Tetenov, Ivan Yudin, Dmitrii Drozdov

item.title: Contractibility of the Gromov--Hausdorff cloud of a normed space
item.description: arXiv:2605.19680v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the Gromov--Hausdorff cloud of every real or complex normed space $X$ admits a strong deformation retraction onto the point represented by $X$.
item.dc:creator: Ivan N. Mikhailov

item.title: Boundary Layers and Finite-Section Asymptotics for Small Polygons
item.description: arXiv:2608.16691v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In large even polygons of unit diameter, computed angle profiles oscillate near the vertex carrying the pendant diameter. We study the half-line variational problem behind this observation of Bingane and Mossinghoff. Its unique positive equilibrium approaches the regular state with alternating multiplier $(-3+\sqrt5)/2$. We determine the sharp energy errors for two ways of closing a finite section and enclose the limiting cubic coefficient in a rational interval of width below $9.4\times10^{-29}$. An explicit scaling identifies these energies with the cubic coefficients of the finite polygon constructions. Transferring the profile to unrestricted area maximizers is a further, conditional result: under the stated geometric hypothesis, the profile gives the $n^{-3}$ term of their maximal area. The recurrence, its finite-section estimates and the enclosure can be checked independently of that hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Dawid Trela

item.title: Affine dual Minkowski problem for general measures
item.description: arXiv:2609.20003v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2025, the affine dual curvature measures $\widetilde{C}_m^a(K,\cdot)$ of convex body $K$ were introduced by Cai, Leng, Wu, and Xi, and the even Minkowski problem for the affine dual curvature measures was solved. In this paper, the necessary and sufficient condition of affine dual Minkowski problem for general measures with $m>1$ are proposed.
item.dc:creator: Hailin Jin, Cheng Zhang

item.title: A proof of the Reinhardt conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.21470v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the Reinhardt conjecture: among centrally symmetric convex disks in the plane, the smoothed regular octagon has the least optimal lattice packing density, and equality holds precisely for its nonsingular affine images. Local cost inequalities reduce arbitrarily long switching cycles of a minimizer to six types. We exclude those types by geometric comparisons and rigorous finite verification, and identify the remaining short minimizer.
item.dc:creator: Fei Xue

item.title: Examples of Ricci limit spaces with infinite holes
item.description: arXiv:2404.00619v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $n\geq 3$, $\lambda \in \mathbb{R} $, and $(X,h)$ be an $n$-dimensional smooth complete Riemannian manifold with ${\rm Ric}_h > \lambda $. In this paper, we construct, for each given $\epsilon >0$, a sequence of $(n+2)$-dimensional manifolds $(M_{i} ,g_i ) \stackrel{GH}{\longrightarrow} (X_\epsilon ,d_\epsilon ) $ with ${\rm Ric}_{g_i} > \lambda $, such that $d_{GH} (X,X_\epsilon ) \leq \epsilon $, and $X_\epsilon $ is homeomorphic to the space obtained by removing an infinite number of balls from $X$. Hence $X_\epsilon $ has dense boundary with an infinite number of connected components. Moreover, $X_\epsilon $ has no open subset which is topologically a manifold. This generalizes Hupp-Naber-Wang's result (arxiv: 2308.03909) from $4$-dimensional case to the general case of dimension $n\geq 3$. Our construction differs from that of Hupp-Naber-Wang. In their approach, Hupp-Naber-Wang considered doing an infinite number of blow-ups on the local complex surface structure of $X$, thus relying on the $4$-dimensional condition. However, our method involves removing an infinite number of balls from $X$, allowing us to construct in the general case of dimensions greater than or equal to $3$. As a corollary, we provide a solution to an open problem posed by Naber in the $3$-dimensional case.
item.dc:creator: Shengxuan Zhou

item.title: Spectral gaps and uniqueness in the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem
item.description: arXiv:2509.08588v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $p<-n$. We prove that a smooth strictly convex solution $K$ is the unit ball if the second non-zero eigenvalue of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator satisfies $\lambda_2(-L_K)\ge\frac{-p-1}{n-1}$. We also derive a lower bound for $\lambda_2(-L_K)$ in terms of concentric inner and outer ellipsoids and give improved bounds for origin-centred and origin-symmetric bodies. Combined with a weighted centroid identity for the polar body, these estimates yield an explicit $\varepsilon_n>0$ for which the unit ball is the only solution when $-n-\varepsilon_n\le p<-n$.
item.dc:creator: Yao Wan

item.title: A Lower Bound on the Sliced Wasserstein Comparison Constant for Translated Measures
item.description: arXiv:2607.26399v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide closed-form expressions for standard 1-Wasserstein distance ($W_1$) and Sliced 1-Wasserstein distance ($SW_1$) for translated probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Furthermore, we construct an explicit lower bound for the constant $c_d$ established by Carlier, Figalli, M\'erigot, and Wang between $W_1$ and $SW_1$ [1] for translated probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Sliced Wasserstein distances are computationally efficient and used in image generation and other applications, which raises natural questions in computational efficiency versus theoretical correctness. A lower bound on the constant $c_d$ gives information about the cost of that efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Avery Noroozi

item.title: Bounded Ratios of Lorentzian Polynomials II: Quadratic Derivatives
item.description: arXiv:2609.07098v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study bounded monomial ratios for Lorentzian polynomials. We prove that, in degree $d\geq2$ and $n$ variables, the bounded ratios from quadratic derivatives generate all bounded ratios for every $M$-convex support if and only if $n\leq3$, $d=2$, or $(n,d)=(4,3)$. For four-variable cubics, the proof uses a decomposition into $M$-concave functions. We construct explicit counterexamples with full support for four-variable quartics and five-variable cubics, then extend these two examples to all remaining pairs.
item.dc:creator: Dijia Chen, Bowen Gan, Ivy Liu, Zemeng Wang, Chengzhi Wu

item.title: The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex
item.description: arXiv:2609.30310v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A polyhex is a connected set of n cells of the regular hexagonal tiling, joined edge to edge, where each cell has area one. Kurz conjectured an upper bound for the area of the convex hull of a polyhex, after the corresponding problem for squares was solved. We prove that the convex hull of a polyhex with n cells has area at most one sixth of the ceiling of $n^2+14n/3$, and that for every n this value is attained by a path made of three straight runs of nearly equal length. This proves the conjecture of Kurz and improves his bound by 1/6 when n is divisible by 3. The proof bounds the hull of the cell centres and three of its widths with a spanning tree of the polyhex. The upper bound is formalised in the Lean 4 proof assistant with the Mathlib library. We also show that for every n the extremal polyhex is unique up to rotation, reflection and translation, which an exhaustive search had confirmed for at most 12 cells. The proof of uniqueness was generated by Claude at the request of Sascha Kurz, and it is also formalised in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Pragyaan Gaur

item.title: Nowhere Locally Metric-Minimising Saddle Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.10908v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the relation between the saddle property and local metric minimality for smooth surfaces in Euclidean spaces. Anton Petrunin and Stephan Stadler proved that every smooth strictly saddle surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is locally metric-minimising and expressed the expectation that this phenomenon fails in $\mathbb{R}^4$. We confirm this expectation and prove a stronger density result: Every smooth strictly saddle embedding of a closed disc into $\mathbb{R}^4$ can be approximated arbitrarily closely in the $C^\infty$-topology by smooth strictly saddle embeddings that are nowhere locally metric-minimising. In particular, nowhere locally metric-minimising saddle embeddings exist in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for every $d \geq 4$. The main ingredient is the construction of non-trivial infinitesimal isometric deformations of saddle immersions in $\mathbb{R}^4$ supported in arbitrarily small discs. We also provide an explicit twisted quadratic surface that is saddle in a neighbourhood of the origin but fails to be locally metric-minimising there, by deriving a necessary condition for metric minimality.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Christian Kohlmeier

item.title: Nearly Sharp Uniform Projection Bounds and Superlinear Vitushkin Inequalities for Deterministic Self-Similar Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.22908v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For all integers $1 \le k < d$ and every $\alpha \in (0,1)$, we construct an explicit deterministic finite homogeneous iterated function system of similarities in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space satisfying the open set condition. The same system is used at every scale. Its attractor $F_{k,\alpha}$ has positive and finite $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Write $A_\delta$ for the closed $\delta$-neighbourhood of a set $A$. For all sufficiently small $\delta > 0$, every orthogonal projection of $(F_{k,\alpha})_\delta$ onto a $k$-plane has $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure at most $C_{k,\alpha}(\log(1/\delta))^{-\alpha}$. The construction places the product of a planar self-similar set $E_\alpha$ and the unit $(k-1)$-cube in a coordinate $(k+1)$-plane. For every $0 < \delta < 1$, the supremum of these projected measures is comparable, up to constants depending only on $k$, to the supremum of the lengths of the orthogonal projections of $(E_\alpha)_\delta$ onto lines. We bound this latter supremum by $C_\alpha(\log(1/\delta))^{-\alpha}$ for all sufficiently small $\delta > 0$. We also prove that the analytic capacity $\gamma((E_\alpha)_\delta)$ is comparable to $(\log(1/\delta))^{-1/2}$ for all sufficiently small $\delta > 0$, with constants depending only on $\alpha$. Consequently, the Favard length of $(E_\alpha)_\delta$ is at most $C_\alpha\gamma((E_\alpha)_\delta)^{2\alpha}$ for every $0 < \delta < 1$. This quantitative Vitushkin inequality is superlinear for $\alpha > 1/2$, and its exponent $2\alpha$ approaches the optimal upper limit of two for this class of self-similar sets as $\alpha$ tends to one.
item.dc:creator: Kaining Jia, Layna Mangiapanello, Caleb Marshall, Victoria Risner

item.title: Constructions and reductions on the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23785v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate five open problems concerning the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations posed by Marinescu and Niculescu. We give constructive answers to three of them. First, we construct an equivalent norm on $\ell^2$ with no three-dimensional Hornich-Hlawka subspace. Second, we present a Nakano space that is not Hornich-Hlawka. Third, we show that the $\alpha$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality fails to hold on nonzero normed spaces when $\alpha \in (1, 2) \cup (2, \infty)$. This implies that on every nonzero inner product space, the $\alpha$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality holds for all triples precisely when $\alpha \in (0,1] \cup \{2\}$. For the remaining two problems, we establish reductions. We prove that $\ell^p(N)$ is Hornich-Hlawka for all $N \geq 3$ and $2 < p \leq \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$ if and only if it is Hornich-Hlawka at $N = 3$ and $p = \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$. Finally, for $p(\cdot): (0, 1) \to [1, 2]$ measurable and integers $k \geq 0$, we establish a Sobolev-Nakano equivalence: we prove that $W^{k,p(\cdot)}(0,1)$, equipped with the sum of the Luxemburg norms of its derivatives of orders $0, \ldots, k$, is Hornich-Hlawka if and only if $L^{p(\cdot)}(0,1)$ is Hornich-Hlawka.
item.dc:creator: Seokbin Lee

item.title: Optimal Patrol Widths in the Infinite-Corridor Barrier-Guarding Game
item.description: arXiv:2611.26140v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A guard of speed at most one and capture radius $r$ patrols an infinite corridor. An intruder knows the patrol and can follow any path of speed at most $q$ from one end to the other. We determine where the maximum width permitted by straight wall runners can be guarded against all such paths. Write $W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ for the supremum over patrols with bounded longitudinal excursion and $F(q)=2r\sqrt{1+(3q^2+2q-1)^{-1}}$ for the wall ceiling on $1/3 < q < 1$. A four-leg bowtie attains $F(q)$ exactly for $q_a\le q < 1$, where $0.457892036651 < q_a < 0.457892036652$. For every $1/3 < q < q_a$ the supremum is strictly smaller. As $q$ approaches $q_a$ from below, $F(q)-W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $r(q_a-q)^2$. The lower estimate controls near-optimal patrols uniformly in their period. A rescaled bowtie gives the matching upper estimate. We also prove that periodic patrols give the same supremum as bounded-excursion patrols. For $q\ge1$ the one-way optimum is $r\sqrt{4+q^{-2}}$, a transverse sweep. This sweep is optimal against transit in both directions for $q\ge1/2$. At low speeds, $qW_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)/r$ tends to two, and an explicit ten-leg patrol guards width greater than $(2/q-1.235353)r$ throughout $0 < q\le1/40$. Rational spacetime and flux certificates give finite-speed bounds, including $6.944691333740r < W_{\mathrm{opt}}(1/4)\le8.10r$.
item.dc:creator: Kevin M. Boergens
